title: Research
text: I use tools from quantum information to study how structure, objectivity, and locality can emerge from quantum systems.

title: Research
text:
Objectivity and Quantum Error Correction
Quantum Darwinism asks how many observers can agree on stable, classical facts about a quantum system. My recent work studies this through operator algebra quantum error correction, where objectivity can be phrased as a local recoverability problem.

Algebraic conditions for objectivity
Connections between redundancy, classicality, and recoverable information
Stabilizer-code models and Clifford simulations

title: Research
text:
Quantum Mereology and Emergent Locality
Quantum mereology asks how the parts of a quantum system should be chosen. I am interested in when a choice of degrees of freedom makes a system look local, geometric, or field-like, even if that structure was not obvious from the original description.

Wave packets from spectra
Emergent lattice descriptions
Locality from choices of factorization or mode basis

title: Research
text:
Quantum Gravity and Information
I am broadly interested in how tools from quantum information and error correction can clarify gravitational questions, especially questions about emergence, observables, and the role of subsystems.
This section is a good place to add a short description of future projects, seminar notes, or reading-group material.

title: About
text:
These are belay glasses, they use prisms.



I am a second-year PhD student in physics at Virginia Tech, working with ChunJun Cao.
My research sits around quantum information, quantum foundations, quantum gravity, quantum mereology, and quantum computing. I am especially interested in cases where the right quantum-information language turns a conceptual question into something that can be computed or tested.

arXiv:2606.10004 · 2026


Wave packets from the spectrum
ChunJun Cao, Oliver Friedrich, Marin Girard, Nicolas Loizeau, and Ashmeet Singh
We show how a Hamiltonian can be represented in a basis where dynamics look more local, producing wave-packet behavior and suggesting a route toward quantum mereology for fields.

arXiv:2606.06588 · 2026


Demystifying Objectivity with Operator Algebra Quantum Error Correction
Marin Girard, Gong Cheng, and ChunJun Cao
We connect quantum Darwinism with operator algebra quantum error correction, making objectivity into a local recoverability question and giving computable tools for studying classicality and redundancy.
arXiv







arXiv:2210.04282 · 2022


Relativistic thermodynamics of perfect fluids
Sylvain D. Brechet and Marin C. A. Girard
We develop a covariant thermodynamic description for relativistic perfect fluids, including relativistic continuity equations and transformation laws for thermodynamic quantities.
